note: Trinidad and Tobago, read on the Ministry of Homeland Security's Work Permits page (homelandsecurity.gov.tt, under the Immigration Act, Chapter 18:01) on 2026-10-30. Any non-national seeking employment, for gain or not, needs a work permit, except one entering to work for one period of no more than thirty days in twelve consecutive months (the work engine's days); permits and their extensions are applied for online on TTBizLink only through the employer's corporate organisation, the form signed by employee and employer (work for the sponsor), and a processing fee is paid whose amount the page doesn't give. Where the worker must be isn't stated ('either'). Terms, fees, decision times, the CARICOM skills certificate, permanent residence and naturalisation aren't on the page read.

sources.title: Ministry of Homeland Security, Trinidad and Tobago: Work Permits
sources.said: This service is applicable to any non-national of Trinidad and Tobago who is seeking employment in Trinidad and Tobago, whether for gain or not, and is desirous of obtaining a work permit. ... A person entering Trinidad and Tobago to engage in gainful occupation for one period not exceeding thirty days in every twelve consecutive months, need not apply for a work permit. ... Accessing and applying for a Work Permit can only be done through your Corporate Organization. ... This must be signed by the employee and employer
